articleTitle: Computer Vision Based Estimation of Shrimp Population Density and Size
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Shrimp is one of the most important aquaculture products in Vietnam and it is desired to continuously estimate shrimp population density and size. This paper presents our initial steps in supervising aqua farming based on computer vision techniques. The computer vision system includes U-net segmentation, marker-controlled watershed segmentation, thresholding, contour tracing, etc. Experiment results show that the proposed method can obtain good results in counting shrimps (mean absolute error of 0.093) and estimating shrimp lengths (RMS error of 0.293 cm) when they are separately located.

articleTitle: A 35–37 GHz MMIC GaN Low Noise Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: A Ka band Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (MMIC) low noise amplifier (LNA) design is presented. Common source configuration with inductive degeneration was used for all transistors to balance the input match and noise figure (NF). A 4-stage 150nm Gallium Nitride (GaN) LNA has the typical NF of 3.7 dB and the minimum small signal gain of above 19.7 dB over the bandwidth of 35-37 GHz. High linearity is achieved with more than 21.6 dBm output 1 dB compression point (OP1dB) and 22.7 dBm saturated output power (Psat). The Ka band LNA has the die dimension of 4340x1200 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A consensus sliding mode control for trajectory tracking of multiple manipulators
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: The paper presents a consensus sliding mode control for trajectory tracking problem of multiple manipulators under the presence of the external disturbance. The proposed method is developed based on the consensus protocol technique and sliding mode control. By using the consensus protocol, the synchronous requirement between manipulators is guaranteed. In addition, the sliding mode control guarantee that the tracking issue is satisfied. A Lyapunov approach is used to analyze the effectiveness of the proposed control in detail. Finally, some simulations are conducted in a robot network which includes two 3-DOF manipulators. The results of the proposed control are compared with the previous control method to verify the efficiency of the proposed control.

articleTitle: A Neural-network-based Nonlinear Controller for Robot Manipulators with Gain-learning Ability and Output Constraints
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive robust controller for tracking control problems of robotic manipulators with output constraints. To realize the constrained objective, the controller is designed using a modified backstepping scheme. A neural-network model is employed to deal with uncertain nonlinearities and disturbances inside the system dynamics. To accomplish an asymptotically tracking performance under predefined constraints, both the control gains and the neural-network approximator are self-learnt with nonlinear laws. Effectiveness of the proposed controller is carefully verified by theoretical proofs and comparative simulation results.

articleTitle: Energized IoT devices through RF Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Wireless Power Harvesting (WPH) of scale is the next stage in low power electronics. In this research, we study to energize wirelessly smart Internet of things (IoT) devices. The IoT and WPH offer a solution to encourage the engineers and growth of modern societies building cell blocks. The idea is a solution to electricity all sensors and devices wirelessly from radio frequency (RF) energy. With RF harvesting technology, we upgrade more IoT devices and keep our lives smarter and more relaxed. The vision of future technology is to self-energize and charge any IoT devices without wires. In this paper, a design patch antenna and four-stage voltage multiplier for RF energy harvesting device with microwave energy 2.45 GHz as the input source. The objective of the work scope is to combine wireless power harvesting technology with a smart house. The proposed prototype takes all parameters above to deliver sufficient energy to remote powering the LED bulbs 5 W wirelessly on a distance of more than five meters at the smart Lab. Finally, we conclude that the harvester circuit coupled with patch antenna can power up the bulb, ultimately IoT devices battery-less.

articleTitle: AI and IoT-powered Smart University Campus: Design of Autonomous Waste Management
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: This paper focuses on developing autonomous waste management which helps efficient and optimal collecting and recycling of garbage. Optimized waste management and green energy-based approach lead to less fuel consumption, which eventually cuts off the carbon footprint, making the waste management process eco-friendlier. Specifically, an autonomous truck is utilized to automatically collect garbage from smart bins to a transfer station by means of solar-powered sensor networks, trajectory planning, self-driving car, RFID recognition, etc. To build an autonomous truck and an autonomous bin, we use hardware including Jetson Nano, Arduino, STM32F4 and camera and open source software including OpenCV, TensorFlow, Arduino IDE, Keil C.

articleTitle: An Improved Offset Min-Sum LDPC Decoding Algorithm for 5G New Radio
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: This paper presents an Improved Offset Min-Sum (IOMS) algorithm for Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC) decoders, used in 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> generation (5G) mobile communication. The proposed algorithm IOMS applies a multiplication factor to check-node update information messages. The simulation results show that the proposed IOMS algorithm offers a better error correction performance than the existing Min-Sum-based algorithms at the expense of a slight increase in complexity. At the BER of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">–5</sup>, the IOMS achieves a decoding gain of 0.1dB with respect to the OMS algorithm.

articleTitle: Variable Pulse Density Modulation for Induction Heating
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Induction heating enables the conversion of electrical energy to thermal energy with a fast, high conversion efficiency and the ability to partially heat be used in a wide variety of welding industries. Conventional diode/SCR rectifiers and mid-frequency/high-frequency resonant inverters used to power conventional induction heaters will have low efficiency, low input power factor, high THD input current. Recently, a research has been done on a current fed three phase-three switch PWM rectifier, producing high power factor but also high current THD. The paper proposes a voltage fed three phase-three switch PWM rectifier with simple structure and control to achieve high power factor and lower current THD. A new variable pulse density modulation without online calculation has been proposed. The preliminary simulation and experimental results verify the feasibility and efficiency of the proposed configuration.

articleTitle: GAN-based Thermal Infrared Image Colorization for Enhancing Object Identification
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Colorizing a thermal infrared image is considered as a challenging task in computer vision and particularly in object recognition. The solution for thermal infrared colorization is quite problematic that not only transforming a grayscale to RGB image where the chrominance is predicted from the given luminance, but also the luminance should be estimated as well. In this paper, we propose a GAN-based method to encourage the similarity and well preserve details of images. Also, we deploy a multi-term objective function including content, perceptual, total variation, relativistic GAN losses and DSSIM to enhance the generated RGB images. Quantitative and qualitative experiments on a large available dataset show that our method obtains impressive results and outperforms compared to others existing colorized methods.

articleTitle: Four In-Wheel BLDC Motors Speed Control in EV Based on Hybrid Fuzzy-PI Controller Visual on GUI
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Recently, the increasing of usage transportation is impacted by air pollution caused by conventional vehicles which are driven by an internal combustion engine (ICE). The novel vehicle's research is to replace that engine with an electric motor, it is called Electric Vehicle (EV). This paper demonstrated a strategy of independent speed steering control for four in-wheels direct drive using brushless DC (BLDC) motors when the EV drives on a straight or curved road. A geometry model of the vehicle named Ackermann-Jeantand steering model is introduced to extract each wheel rotating speeds to avoid the wheel slide with the road during the EV operates on a corner street. The hybrid fuzzy-PI controller is used as a speed controller for each motor in the model in this design. The results are also compared with PI and fuzzy logic controllers. The results of two different modes have been illustrated on GUI with a satisfied response; thus, the control system has functioned correctly. It is revealed that the EV is driven and steered safely on the road.

articleTitle: An Improved Model-Free Predictive Current Control Strategy with Stagnant Current Variation Update Reduction
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Model-free predictive current control (MFPCC) is emerging as a powerful strategy to control voltage source inverters (VSIs) without the knowledge of the system parameters. However, the output current performance may be deteriorated significantly due to the stagnant current variation update in the conventional MFPCC. To improve the output current performance, this paper proposes a simple MFPCC strategy to keep updated all current variations of the VSI. Each current variation is firstly separated into two parts, and then each part is updated frequently using the two most recent measured current variations and their applied voltage vectors, respectively. Because the stagnant current variation update is effectively reduced in the proposed method, the output current performance with the proposed method is improved significantly compared to that with the conventional MFPCC. Experimental results are given to verify the effectiveness of the proposed MFPCC.

articleTitle: Investigation of Effects of Rising and Falling Time, Ringing Phenomena and Dead Time in GaN Inverter on Iron Loss with Very High Sampling Rate
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Although general impacts of the ringing phenomena occurring at dozens of megahertz and the rapid rising time in several nanoseconds in voltage waveform of the gallium nitride-field effect transistor (GaN-FET) inverter on the iron loss in ring core tests were considered in some recent studies, those works only used oscilloscopes with a medium sampling rate (e.g. 100 MS/s), which may cause the analysis and evaluation to be not really sufficient and correct. Hence, our paper investigates the detailed relations and effects of the rising time, falling time, ringing phenomena and voltage spike at many pulses in voltage waveform on the iron loss in a ring core under the GaN-FET inverter excitation using a top-notch oscilloscope with a very high sampling rate of 10 GS/s for measurement. Furthermore, the unique characteristics of the input current in negative and positive ranges relating to the ringing phenomena are considered as another novelty and contribution of this research. Moreover, the relations between the total harmonic distortions of the magnetic flux density and input current with the iron loss are examined. The effect of large changes in the dead-time of GaN-FET devices on the iron loss of the ring core is also examined.

articleTitle: A $63-\mu \mathrm{W}$ 92.68-dB SNDR Sigma-Delta Modulator using Self-biased Inverter-based Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: This paper presents an inverter-based sigma-delta modulator for use in wearable devices. This work employs the use of power-efficient integrators using self-biased, fully differential inverters, allowing for the amplifier to compensate any fluctuation due to process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) variations. To verify the effectiveness of the amplifier, a second-order discrete-time sigma-delta modulator is implemented in 0.18μm CMOS technology. The modulator achieves a 92.68 dB SNDR and 93.47 dB SNR while consuming 63-μW from a 1.8V supply, corresponding to a Walden's FOM of 89.96 fJ/step for a signal bandwidth of 10 kHz.

articleTitle: Applying Kalman filter to UWB positioning with DS-TWR method in LOS/NLOS scenarios
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: In this paper, a Kalman Filter is proposed to overcome the errors in Non-Line-Of-Sight environment and improve the accuracy of Double-Side Two-way ranging and trilateration localization results in both Line-Of-Sight and Non-Line-Of-Sight scenarios. The study is applied on the Decawave DMW1001 module. The results indicate that Kalman Filter can be used to enhance the indoor positioning system using DS-TWR and trilateration method, and the best improvement of error is 18.18% in the localization phase of LOS environment.

articleTitle: Computer Vision System for Reading Analog Gauges at Power Substation
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: This paper proposes a computer vision system for reading analog gauges at a power substation. The gauges mentioned in this paper include oil level gauges, winding temperature gauges and SF6 gas density gauges. We present two different algorithms since an oil level gauge has different characteristics from a winding temperature gauge or an SF6 gas density gauge. For the oil level gauge, a color segmentation method is used to detect the pointer. Then we use Canny Edge Detector in combination with the Hough Circle Transform method to detect scale marks. Based on the position of the pointer and the marks, we detect the indicating value of the gauge. For winding temperature gauges and SF6 gas density gauges, we find the direction of the pointer based on the geometry properties of a double-edged pointer. With this information, we can calculate the value indicated on the gauge face using interpolation between the direction of the pointer and the value of the gauge. The system error is almost zero in case of an oil level gauge and remains low in the case of a winding temperature gauge and an SF6 gas density gauge. Mobile robots integrated with this computer vision system will work faster and more accurately than humans and will also help avoid dangerous accidents.

articleTitle: A broadband, high even-order suppression distributed power amplifier for sub-6 GHz communication system
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: A high power level with high even-order suppression over the broadband power amplifier is presented. In this study, the multi-octave bandwidth is achieved with the use of a distributed architecture. Besides, with the presence of the balun, a high power level is achieved with even-order suppression properties. The design is fabricated using a 450 nm Gallium Nitride (GaN) process with a bare-die size of 4.5 mm * 3 mm. The EM simulated results in the 2-6 GHz band show that the PA exhibits a minimum linear gain of 10.8 dB, with the saturated output power of 44.6 dBm (28W). The 2nd harmonic rejection level is at least -33 dBc.

articleTitle: Combined Equalizer Based on Switch-matrix and Bi-directional Converter for Parallel-Connected Battery Packs in Data-Center or Telecommunication
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: In data-center and telecommunication applications, the battery energy storage system is utilized to ensure operational stability. Battery packs are connected in parallel to enlarge the system capacity, and the hot-swap process is adopted to avoid power interruption. However, the battery inconsistency causes an unequal current sharing issue between branches and the hot-swap process makes that issue more serious. This paper proposes a combined equalizer based on the switch-matrix and bi-directional converter to balance the energy between battery packs, and an equalization strategy is presented to improve the limitation of the hot-swap process. The simulation results verify that the SOC of battery packs are equalized within 0.5% in both idle and non-idle modes while the branch currents are confined in the safety level. Besides, the proposed equalization strategy overcomes the inrush current issue in the hot-swap process when the battery pack is replaced and connected to the DC bus.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave Antenna Selection Switch using Advanced CMOS Technologies
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Intended to be the on-chip CMOS-based switching circuit for the fifth generation (5G) mobile communication equipment. The proposed switches were fabricated using GlobalFoundries 45nm SOI CMOS (45RFSOI) process. The two single-pole double-throw (SPDT) switches are designed and optimized with asymmetric structure in order to reduce the insertion loss on the transmitter side while maintain high isolation on the receiver side. The first SPDT is controlled by +/- 1V when the second SPDT with cross-biasing technique using 0 and 1V for the voltage control. The measured performance of both designs indicates that the chip can achieve the insertion loss lower than 1dB and the isolation higher 20dB at 28GHz.

articleTitle: Advanced Grid Voltage Synchronization Method Under Abnormal Grid Conditions
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: In this paper, a novel estimation of the grid voltage using the dual enhanced SOGI-enhanced FLL (eSOGI-eFLL) structure is proposed. In eSOGI, a variable feedback gain is added to provide the required degree of freedom, thus the fast response of eSOGI is achieved. Moreover, to improve the estimation performance, the eFLL output is modified with an additional compensation component which is found from eFLL input and new gain. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by the simulation results under various grid fault events, such as voltage sag, phase angle jump, and step change in grid frequency.

articleTitle: Security for Jamming-Aided Energy Harvesting Cognitive Radio Networks
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: We investigate cognitive radio networks where the unlicensed sender operates in the overlay mode to relay the information of the licensed transmitter as well as send its individual information. To secure information broadcasted by the unlicensed sender against the wire-tapper, we invoke jammers to limit eavesdropping. Also, to exploit efficiently radio frequency energy in licensed signals, we propose the unlicensed sender and all jammers to scavenge this energy source. To assess the security measures of both licensed and unlicensed networks, we first derive rigorous closed-form formulas of licensed/unlicensed secrecy outage probabilities. Next, we validate these formulas with Monte-Carlo simulations before using them to achieve insights into the security capability of the proposed jamming-aided energy harvesting cognitive radio networks in crucial system parameters.

articleTitle: Novel Method for Key Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: To ensure for the security of PKI users' private keys, a new method for accessing and storing private keys is proposed in this article. Using advanced features of watermarking and symmetric encryption, the shared private key slices are encrypted and stored in different boxes, and the entire private key is reconstructed as long as the boxes are effective. The secure performance of storing and accessing private keys is also presented in the scheme. At the same time, the legal users can be verified by system using biometric or signature authentication.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Reluctance-Based Synchronous Motors Consider for Electric Scooter
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: This paper performs the performance comparison between a SynRM and its three variations that changing the number of turns, the number of poles, and adding low-cost PM, i.e., ferrite. The comparison is conducted by finite element analysis (FEA). From these analyses, the trending of performance of reluctance-based synchronous motor consider for electric scooter is presented. Adding low-cost PM can increase torque and efficiency of motor at both low- and highspeed ranges while the changing of the number of turns or number of poles cannot well improve the motor performance. As a result, PMa-SynRM with low-cost PM is a good choice for the electric scooter application.

articleTitle: Bottled Water Classification Using Spectroscopy and Deep Belief Network
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Neural networks and their variations have been widely applied to classification problems. Among them, the classification of mixtures using neural networks has been investigated by experts from both signal processing and chemical fields. However, the extracted features of beverages such as water, soft drinks, and alcohols, are usually highly collinear. Therefore, traditional methods or simple artificial neural networks may not yield the most accurate results. In this article, several steps were introduced to improve the classification accuracy. Firstly, proper system design and measurement methods were used to mitigate errors. Secondly, deep belief network was applied to adapt to the non-linearity and collinear of features. Finally, suitable learning method was selected. As a result, our system could classify samples from various bottled water branches with nearly 100% accuracy.

articleTitle: Utilizing Mean Correlation of Accelerometer Components in Counting Strides
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Smartwatch with health tracking is essential for everyone in their daily workouts in which the information step count is helpful for developing services to smartwatch users, e.g. distance, pace. In addition, people who track their daily steps may not only be more active, they may also be less likely to develop health problems that lead to events like heart attacks or broken bones. Built-in MEMS motion sensors, the smartwatch continuously senses the movements of the arm on a 3-axis accelerometer. Cyclic nature of human walking results in cyclic signals. The concept of correlation is to measure how similar two time-series cycles are. Misinterpreting the correlation value results in undercounting or overcounting the number of steps. In this paper, a mean correlation is constructed from all three accelerometer data and its features are analyzed comprehensively. High precision of stride classification is achieved in practical scenarios in terms of true positive rates and true negative rates. The algorithm accuracy has been found 99.03% that is stable with arbitrary orientation of the smartwatch.

articleTitle: Feature Extraction Using Neural Networks for Vietnamese Text Classification
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: In this paper, a feature extraction method based on neural networks for Vietnamese text classification is developed. The Vietnamese online news documents are initially preprocessed to transform to lower-case documents as well as remove punctuation and stop-words. Then, the tokenization applying the combination of uni-gram and bi-gram models is conducted to generate a list of tokens for each document. As a result, polyphonic linguistic problems in Vietnamese language are diminished. The statistical term frequency - inverse document frequency model is employed to represent the lists of tokens as real value vectors. Instead of applying conventional feature selection algorithms, neural networks are conducted for dimensionality reduction. Therefore, not only the size of the term frequency - inverse document frequency vectors are reduced, but also distinctive feature vectors are created for text classification tasks. Support vector machines are utilized in the classification step. The results attained in the experiment have shown that our work using neural networks for the feature extraction outperforms other traditional methods.

articleTitle: Adaptive Switching Controller: A New Design of Dual Prescribed Sliding Surface and PID for Vibration Control
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: In this study, a new design of adaptive switching controller is presented. A dual sliding surface of sliding mode control and a modified Riccati-like equation of optimal control are combined as a hybrid controller for vibration. The interval type 2 fuzzy model is also embedded in the proposed control for uncertainty. The proposed control is simulated in the suspension system featuring smart damper with magnetorheological fluid (MR). Simulation results show that the proposed control is good performance and can use for real system.

articleTitle: Modeling Ka-Band Radar System to Characterize the EM Wave Propagation Properties in the Application of Target Detection
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Ground target detection and identification using radar system in disparate environments has been a topic of enduring interest. Different radar bands have dominances for diverse environmental conditions. For example, it has been shown that the propagation characteristics of millimeter waves make them appropriate for a variety of applications including transmitting bulks of computer data, radar or satellite communications. By dispatching signals from a directional transmitter, reflecting waves against the concealed object and back, the radar would be able to figure out whether if there is an object behind and its distance. A meticulous study on the properties of the EM wave propagation is conducted to determine the significant parameters that affect the performance capability of radar system. Experiments are also carried out to justify the results obtained from the study.

articleTitle: Evaluation and Improvement Distribution actual network Reliability using ETAP
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: In this day and age, supplying electricity for an entire nation during the Industry 4.0 era is not a simple mission. Therefore, the power system reliability must be one step ahead. Troubles related to the Distribution network reliability are considered the most important for they directly affect the customers. Many latest technologies are often applied to effectively operate this sort of network. The most difficult Distribution network reliability problem is its vastness and complexity that makes manual calculation seem impossible. However, thanks to the modernization of Electrical engineering software, these issues are now easily solved. This paper briefly introduces the Distribution network reliability and proposes a method to establish an optimal plan to improve the reliability by using the ETAP's Reliability function. The research applies ETAP in evaluating the reliability of an actual network to find out its deficiencies. Based on this, we can propose manners to improve this network reliability. Finally, we verify the effectiveness of these manners through economic indicators.

Author Keywords: ETAP's Reliability function for an actual network
Distribution network reliability improvement with ETAP

articleTitle: A $3.86\ \mu \mathrm{W}$ Miller-Compensated Inverter Transimpedance Amplifier for Photoplethysmography Sensing
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: This paper presents a design and simulation results of an ultra-low power inverter transimpedance amplifier. Transimpedance amplifiers require negative feedback, hence, stability should always be maintained. The design was able to achieve a 92.9 dB transimpedance gain, 81.77 pARMS total input integrated noise from 0 to 10 KHZ, 2% total harmonic distortion, and 88 dB spurious-free dynamic range. The Miller capacitances were used to ensure stability by separating the poles and removing the region of instability. The circuit was implemented in 0.18 μm technology with 1.2 V supply and a power dissipation of 3.86 μW.

articleTitle: Machinery Monitoring and Maintenance System Using Decision Tree Model for Fault Prediction
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: This paper presents a design and implementation of the machinery monitoring and maintenance system. The proposed system has two advanced features including supervision of machinery in real-time and potential fault prediction by using decision tree model. The monitoring system is designed using IoT technologies to collect machine data including power consumption and operation states. Moreover, the potential faults of monitored machines are predicted by the proposed algorithm using decision tree model. The whole system has been implemented and applied in a real factory to demonstrate its performance.

articleTitle: Implementation of Carrier-Cancellation Circuit for UHF RFID Reader RF Front-End using Genetic Algorithm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: A problem of ultra-high frequency radiofrequency identification (UHF RFID) reader is the reading range because one antenna is used for transmitting carrier and backscattered signal. In this study, a carrier-cancellation circuit is used with a commercial directional coupler to obtain a good isolation between transmitter (Tx) and receiver (Rx) by suppressing the transmitting leakage signal. The suppression level of the circuit can be obtained by applying the Genetic Algorithm (GA) to optimize values of digitally tunable capacitors. Experimental result of the S24 of the directional coupler is approximately of -70 dB which showed the good isolation between Tx and Rx at 900 MHz.

articleTitle: Research on trial production of lithium-ion battery with positive electrode by doping of Al fibers
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are required to have a stable and thick coating on the positive and negative electrode sheets. The coater bar for adjusting the coating thickness has a limit in manufacturing, and it is impossible to increase the coating thickness indefinitely. By increasing the coating thickness of the slurry, battery capacity can be effectively increased. In mass slurry coating production factories, there are two methods, one is to use a coater bar on a small scale and the other is to apply with nozzle to the current collector at the mass production level. In each method, trial and error has been made to increase the coating thickness.

articleTitle: Application of Image Processing Technology to Determine Building Structure Vibration
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Recently, structure vibration determination using camera image has been received wide attention. Most contributions on this area use a remote camera to directly observe an object, and calculate the oscillation based on the change of a point on object picture. This method has its advantages, but there are still unresolved problems such as image noise, low quality due to low light level. Based on image processing too but with a completely new approach, the vibration measurement system described in this paper really deal with the problem by using observing a light spot lighted directly to object from distance. Furthermore, an estimation method for the measurement resolution and error is proposed to increase the precise of the vibration displacement measurement of the building and transport structures. The accuracy of the proposed method is described and validated along with selected experimental results.

articleTitle: LoRa Gateway Based on SoC FPGA Platforms
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: The term Internet of Things (IoT) is increasingly popular and is seen as the essential infrastructure used in many fields. In particular, LoRa (Long Range) is gradually becoming the first choice for long-range, low-energy communication. The LoRaWAN system implementation on the available platforms (The Things Network, ChirpStack Network Server) has certain limitations depending on the Internet. In this article, we build a single channel LoRa gateway on the SoC FPGA platforms but still keep, namely, applying the power of ARM cortex A9 core on DE10-Nano and the customizability of FPGA to build general AES-128 core for security: authentication and encryption. Adopt the DMA technique for AES-128 to achieve high bandwidth. Specifically, DMA for the AES-128 core operating at 150 MHz frequency achieves 1200 Mbps bandwidth and take up 17% resources. Besides, the bandwidth of the gateway's handling is 115.6 Kbps with ARM cortex A9 at the clock of 800Mbps.

articleTitle: Proactive Allocation of Radio Resources to Enhance Service Continuity in Cellular Networks
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Mobile communication is one of the most widely used technologies in today's world, which is on the verge of its fifth-generation (5G). Mobile broadband services are frequently availed by users (e.g., vehicular infotainment) on the go. Providing a consistent service quality to the user despite his mobility is a key challenge for network operators. The cellular service area is often associated with coverage holes, where the received signal quality is too poor to maintain a desired service quality. Further, deep shadowed holes would lead to signal loss and service interruption. Acquiring beforehand knowledge of a user encountering a coverage hole in his near future will be beneficial in designing smart resource allocation schemes. In this paper, a proactive allocation of radio resources is presented based on the forecast of a coverage hole in the user's immediate route. A Markov model enhanced with the start and terminus information of a user is used for the prediction. The user anticipated to experience a coverage hole imminently is allocated more resources appropriately and data buffering is facilitated. The simulation results show a significant improvement in user throughput and a major reduction in service interruption (for streaming service) while traversing routes associated with coverage holes. Further, this paper also highlights recent advancements in the 5G system (5GS) architecture that are vital for the deployment of the presented scheme and associated data analytics.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Framework Applied For Predicting Anomaly of Respiratory Sounds
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: This paper proposes a robust deep learning framework used for classifying anomaly of respiratory cycles. Initially, our framework starts with front-end feature extraction step. This step aims to transform the respiratory input sound into a two-dimensional spectrogram where both spectral and temporal features are well presented. Next, an ensemble of C-DNN and Autoencoder networks is then applied to classify into four categories of respiratory anomaly cycles. In this work, we conducted experiments over 2017 Internal Conference on Biomedical Health Informatics (ICBHI) benchmark dataset. As a result, we achieve competitive performances with ICBHI average score of 0.49, ICBHI harmonic score of 0.42.

articleTitle: Citrus Leaf Disease Detection and Classification Using Hierarchical Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: In this paper, an effective framework is proposed to classify four types of citrus leaf diseases out of healthy leaves through leaf features inspection. Four considered citrus leaf diseases are canker, sooty mold, greening and leaf-miner. Our framework consists of three main stages of pre-processing, feature extraction and classification. Since image analysis of citrus leaf disease is based on texture, color and shape features through leaf region, the region of main leaf is first segmented from the complex background in the pre-processing stage. Then leaf features are extracted in different color spaces and prominent ones are chosen based on feature distribution analysis. The selected features are fed to the SVM classification stage to detect and classify the diseases. In our study, we propose a hierarchical SVM classification model based on leaf features analysis to improve the accuracy rate. The numerical results prove the effectiveness of our proposed hierarchical SVM model over the multi-class SVM model. Our proposed hierarchical SVM model gives the infected leaf detection rate of 92.5%, and a high accuracy rate of 91.76%.

articleTitle: Multi-View Digital Mammography Mass Classification: A Convolutional Neural Network Model Approach
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the breast. Among various breast screening techniques, mammography is the current gold standard for early detection of BC. In this paper, a two-stage breast mass classification model is innovatively proposed. In specific, stage-one is a feature extraction stage in which mammogram features are extracted and selected by a pre-trained convolutional neural network (CNN) model. Then, in stage-two, CNN-extracted mammogram features are classified as benign or malignant cases by a two-layered neural network classifier. Our proposed method has been evaluated on the subset of the INbreast database. The results show that our model obtains better performance than previous advanced classification methods.

articleTitle: S11 Calculation for a Coaxial-loaded-type Stepped Cut-off Circular Waveguide by the Moment Method
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: A formula for calculating the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{S}_{\mathbf{11}}$</tex> value of a stepped circular waveguide with a coaxial feed was formulated using the method of moments (MoM). The analytical model for the formulation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{S}_{\mathbf{11}}$</tex> calculation was assumed with 1. no sample inserted (open) and 2. pure water inserted. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{S}_{\mathbf{11}}$</tex> for the analytical model was calculated at frequencies of 0.50, 1.5 and 3.0 GHz. The MoM-calculated <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{S}_{\mathbf{11}}$</tex> values were compared with those calculated using the mode-matching technique (MMT) and the finite element method (FEM). The MoM values corresponded closely to the MMT values and the FEM values, even though the inner diameter of the circular cavity was slightly larger than the inner diameter of the outer conductor for the coaxial line. The formulation of the equation for the analytical model was thus validated.

articleTitle: A Reliable Approach to Secure IoT Systems Using Cryptosystems Based on SoC FPGA Platforms
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: The use of cryptography algorithms based on hardware to protect the security and privacy of the loT systems is in huge demand. However, hardware-based security systems are similar to software-based in that they can be attacked by a type of malicious code called malware. In this article, we used the self-applied cryptography algorithm on the hardware-based to protect the data security of loT systems, and that gives the trustee than using software-based of hardware-based inform of ASIC chip. Detailly, we have developed an SoC FPGA system including main factors are a built-in ARM processor core, a self-implemented IP core acting as 128-bit AES co-processors, and SDRAM memory. Furthermore, this system has been placed on the DE10-Standard board and ran with an application in Linux operations. Besides, we have applied the DMA technique to obtain high-speed data transfer. As a result, our cryptosystem is compact and can achieve high performance with low frequencies. Details, the DMA Controller and 128-bit AES IP core operate at a frequency of 150 MHz, and they can reach the speed of 1200 Mbps and above 700 Mbps, respectively.

articleTitle: Robust Blind Watermarking against Geometrical Attacks with Medical Images for EMR/EHR
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: In this paper, an efficient solution for robust watermarking against geometrical attacks with medical images is proposed. In the embedding process, at first, we select the robust non-overlapping Scale-Invariant Feature Transform regions. Then, we embed the same information into these regions by using the even-odd quantization technique. In the extraction process, blind recovery of information is performed by exploiting the correlation among all detection regions. Both fan-shaped and half-ring-shaped regions are suggested for multi-bit watermarking. The embedded image quality is analyzed and compared to other image watermarking approaches based on Spread Spectrum or Least Significant Bit techniques. The reliability and the robustness are investigated with various geometrical attacks such as rotation, scaling and cropping. Moreover, our solution is also better than existing methods in terms of usefulness and security for electronic medical/health record applications.

articleTitle: Hardware Implementation For Fast Block Generator Of Litecoin Blockchain System
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: The development of blockchain-based cryptocurren-cies has attracted a lot of interest in many fields, especially in academic research. Besides Bitcoin, Litecoin is one of the most popular cryptocurrency based on blockchain currently. The Litecoin mining process uses the Scrypt algorithm as a hash function in Proof-of-Work (PoW) consensus mechanism. The yield of cryptocurrency mining depends a lot on the processing performance of the hardware. Therefore, this paper proposes a hardware design of the Scrypt algorithm in the Litecoin mining system using the Verilog hardware description language (HDL). In the proposed design, the pipeline technique is applied at two levels: the overall Scrypt level and the PBKDF2 level. Additionally, the design is divided into several stages to reduce the latency of each clock cycle and increase the operating frequency. The simulation and verification of the design are performed based on Atlys Spartan-6 FPGA Board and Xilinx Virtex-7 FPGA VC707. The performance of the design evaluated on Atlys Spartan-6 has the hash rate of 2209 hashes/s. The maximum operating frequency of the system is 147.059MHz. On Xilinx Virtex-7, the hash rate of the design reaches 5332 hashes/s and the maximum operating frequency reaches 355.051 MHz.

articleTitle: Transient stability analysis in high photovoltaic penetration scenarios
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: In recent years renewable energy sources (wind and solar energy) have been significantly integrated into the power systems in various countries. In this context the ever increasing penetration of photovoltaic power will have a huge impact on the steady state and transient stability of the grid. However, future power grids are to face the reality that renewable energy sources have the inherently intermittent characteristics of rapidly changing generation capacity depending heavily on weather conditions, along with the reduced inertia of the whole system. This paper analyzed the effects on transient stability of power grids in scenarios with increasing penetration of photovoltaic power plants in terms of analysis of different penetration levels of photovoltaic power plants carried out on an IEEE test power system model. As a result of the analyses, we are able to draw typical conclusions as of the negative impacts of high photovoltaic penetration on the power systems, as well as propose possible potential solutions to the issues of ensuring necessary transient stability.

articleTitle: Online Robust Sliding-Windowed LiDAR SLAM in Natural Environments
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Despite the growing interest for autonomous environmental monitoring, effective SLAM realization in native habitats remains largely unsolved. In this paper, we fill this gap by presenting a novel online graph-based SLAM system for 2D LiDAR sensor in natural environments. By taking advantage of robust weighting scheme, sliding-windowed optimization, fast scan-matcher and parallel computing, our system not only delivers stable performance in cluttered surroundings but also meets real-time constraint. Simulated and experimental results confirm the feasibility and efficiency in the overall design of the proposed system.

articleTitle: Decentralized Capacitor Voltage Control of Flying Capacitor Multilevel Inverter
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: This paper proposes a decentralized capacitor voltage control strategy for the flying capacitor multilevel inverter (FC-MLI) in combination with the decentralized self-aligned phase-shifted pulse width modulation (PWM) (self-aligned carriers) method. For FC-MLI, the capacitor voltage of switching modules requires a special condition of initial capacitor voltage to startup and reach the desired value. To overcome this issue, a decentralized capacitor voltage control algorithm is proposed to regulate the capacitor voltage to the required value under normal operation as well as in case of reconfiguration of the system when the number of switching cells is changed. The key approach is that each switching cell controller of the FC-MLI synchronizes and regulates its own voltage effectively by using information from its neighboring cell controllers. The validity of proposed decentralized capacitor voltage control method in association with the self-aligned phase-shifted carriers is shown by simulation results using Matlab Simulink software.

articleTitle: Torque Ripple Eliminations for Multiphase Nonsinusoidal Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: This paper is to propose a control scheme, a combination of the classical field-oriented control (FOC) technique and artificial intelligence (AI), to obtain constant torques in multiphase non-sinusoidal permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) drives. Higher torque density, easier fabrication, and lower costs are several advantages of non-sinusoidal back electromotive force (back-EMF) machines over sinusoidal ones. However, multi-harmonics existing in back-EMFs possibly generate torque ripples, reducing torque quality of the drive. Therefore, in this paper, an adaptive linear neuron (ADALINE), a simple type of AI, is combined with the classical FOC technique to eliminate these torque ripples. The proposed control scheme is validated by numerical results with a seven-phase PMSM. In addition, these results are compared with an existing strategy to prove its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Environmental Economic Dispatch Using Stochastic Fractal Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: today, the issue of environmental protection is being urgently set. To ensure environmental factors and economic efficiency in the context which fossil energy resources are increasingly scarce, the control of fuel costs and emission costs are crucial factors in ensuring and increase profits of power plants. This paper uses stochastic fractal search algorithm (SFSA) for solving the economic emission dispatch (EED) problems - a multi object optimization problems with load balance, power generation limits, and fuel constraints. The proposed SFSA has been tested on 6-generator of environmental economic and IEEE 30 bus system where the single line diagram is shown in Fig 1. For each test system, the problem is analyzed in two cases of single and multi- objective functions. The obtained results from the test cases have been compared to those from other methods in the literature as evidence for the SFSA can be a new effective method for solving economic emission dispatch problems.

articleTitle: Energy Management and Real-Time Scheduling for Self-Powered Sensors
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Most of wireless sensors are dynamically changing and execute two types of tasks: hard deadline periodic ones and aperiodic ones with no deadline. The emergence of energy harvesting technologies makes it possible to design self-powered sensors through environmental energy. Nevertheless, classical scheduling techniques need to be reconceived so as to take into account the fluctuating energy source and energy consumptions of tasks. Hence, we firstly describe the called TB-H and TB*-H aperiodic task servers which are extensions of the famous Total Bandwidth server. We show how TB-H and TB*-H permit to provide short response times for the aperiodic tasks by computing adequate virtual deadlines taking into account both time and energy constraints. Our second contribution lies in extensive simulations to bring to light the effectiveness of these two novel Bandwidth based servers in comparison to basic background approaches.
